title: Read any field of an order line

blocks.text: The warehouse sends order lines such as `sku=K-204;qty=12;wrap;note=ring twice`. Fields are separated by `;`, and a field is `key=value`, except a flag such as `wrap`, which has no `=` and whose value is the empty string.
`Fields.valueOf(line, key)` already walks the line one field at a time. Finish the two helpers it uses, in `src/main/java/practice/Fields.java`:

items: `fieldEnd(line, from)`: where the field that starts at `from` ends;
`separatorIn(line, from, to)`: the position in `line` of that field's `=`, or -1 when the field is a flag.

blocks.text: Any field must be readable, the last one included, and a key the line doesn't have gives an empty `Optional`. About three lines in total.

cases.says: the value of the first field of a line is found
the last field, which has no ';' after it, is found, and a key the line doesn't have gives an empty result instead of an exception
a field that doesn't start at the beginning of the line is read at the right position
a field without '=' is a flag with an empty value, even when a later field has an '='

origin.section: The Range Form of indexOf Throws Where the Old Form Returned -1

concepts: String.indexOf(ch, begin, end) throws for a range outside the string, including end = -1, and returns an index counted from the start of the string.
